transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

To be honest, I'm here because I feel like I'm constantly on the go and just can't seem to slow down. It honestly feels like I'm being driven by a motor all the time, and sitting still is incredibly difficult for me.
Do you also have trouble focusing, following through on tasks, or frequently make careless mistakes?

No, I wouldn't say I struggle with focusing or making careless mistakes. Once I actually get started on something, I can usually follow through with it just fine. My main issue is really just the constant physical restlessness and needing to be active.
Do you often interrupt others, have trouble waiting your turn, or feel the need to respond before a question is fully asked?

Yes, absolutely. I frequently find myself blurting out answers before the other person has even finished asking their question. It is really hard for me to wait my turn to speak, so I often just jump right in.
Have these symptoms been present since childhood, or did they start more recently?

I've actually been this way since I was a kid, definitely back in elementary school before I was 12. While I've always struggled with this, it has become particularly challenging and noticeable over the last 9 months.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidate was Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation), and the current conversation supports this diagnosis. The patient reports a lifelong history of hyperactive and impulsive symptoms, including feeling 'driven by a motor,' difficulty sitting still, interrupting others, and blurting out answers, with onset before age 12 and persistence into adulthood. There is no indication of inattentive symptoms (e.g., difficulty focusing, careless mistakes), which rules out Combined Presentation, and no symptoms suggestive of mood or psychotic disorders, anxiety disorders, trauma-related disorders, or eating disorders. The recent worsening over the last 9 months does not change the core symptom pattern consistent with Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation. No new candidates are added, and the existing candidate remains strongly supported.
